brief: Goldman's Louis Miller (Global Reflections) says the AI trade has recouped most of Monday's losses and, after a double bottom, has room to grind higher toward a breakout, so he is buying AI on incremental agentic use-case materialization creating alpha on both long and short sides. He is short Consumer Inertia (GSXUSWCH) because AI agents compress the switching costs that used to be booked as a consumer moat, citing Muse's 1.6 million US downloads in 8 days (nearly 2x ChatGPT's pace, per Apptopia) and Thursday's telco selloff (TMUS -5.5%, AT&T -2%, VZ -3%) as evidence; he also runs an ex-financials version (GSCBSWC2). He calls AI power positioning (GSX1POW1) the most washed-out AI theme, expects midterms to support renewables, and is bullish Europe power (GSXERNEW). He is short UK Homebuilders (GSSBUKHO, hit by 20-year-high gilt yields) and UK Consumer (GSXEUKCO, resilient YTD but confidence surveys turning negative), long US Low Income Consumer Discretionary (GSXULOWD) conditional on geopolitical relief, long German fiscal spend (GSXEGFSC, citing planned 2027 defense spend of €140bn, up €31.4bn from 2026) versus a short hedge on French Domestic (GSXEFRDO) into next year's elections.
